 Durée : mandat de longue durée, début prévu en décembre 2026

 Concevoir et mettre en œuvre des architectures d’information d’entreprise (solutions de site, modèles de site, types de contenu, propriétés gérées)

 au moins 2 mandats d’envergure (environ 1 an chacun) d’implantation et de création d’un nouveau SharePoint dans une organisation

 Autonomie, esprit d’équipe, capacité de vulgarisation et excellentes aptitudes en communication

 Expérience de migration vers SharePoint Online / Microsoft 365

 Expérience dans le secteur public québécois

This role focuses on reviewing and validating externally developed designs to ensure they are fit for purpose, meet specifications, and align with sound engineering principles, while liaising with and holding external teams accountable for quality and performance. The Lead provides final technical review and sign-off, bringing deep expertise and experience to the role.
 This role acts as a senior member of the owner’s engineering team and is accountable for ensuring that mechanical design solutions are safe, reliable, operable, maintainable, and aligned with project objectives. The Lead Mechanical Engineer will work closely with internal project engineers and external engineering, EPCM, and equipment vendors to develop fit-for-purpose mechanical designs that support project progression through FEL-2, FEL-3, and FEL-4 detailed engineering, construction, commissioning, and handover.
 The successful candidate will provide technical leadership across mechanical systems including rotating equipment, static equipment, piping, material handling systems, utilities, package equipment, and plant infrastructure, while supporting engineering governance, design reviews, risk management, and value improvement initiatives. This may also include overseeing and/or participating in all HAZOPS and subject matter regulatory reviews.
 Key Responsibilities 
 Lead mechanical engineering activities for capital projects through FEL-2, FEL-3, and some FEL-4 execution planning.
 Serve as the mechanical engineering lead within Cyclic’s owner’s team, ensuring that internal and external engineering deliverables meet project requirements, technical standards, and stage-gate expectations.
 Manage and review the work of external engineering consultants, EP, EPC, EPCM and similar build partners, equipment suppliers, and specialist contractors for mechanical scope.
 Develop and maintain mechanical design criteria, engineering specifications, equipment standards, and discipline deliverables to support project development and execution.
 Provide technical leadership for mechanical systems including rotating equipment, tanks, vessels, heat exchangers, pumps, piping systems, material handling systems, utility systems, and package equipment.
 Review and approve mechanical engineering deliverables such as equipment datasheets, equipment lists, piping and instrumentation diagrams, layouts, mechanical design packages, technical bid evaluations, and vendor documents.
 Support development of plant layouts and equipment arrangements with a focus on constructability, maintainability, operability, accessibility, and safety.
 Participate in and lead discipline input into design reviews, HAZOPs, model reviews, value engineering workshops, risk assessments, and constructability reviews.
 Ensure mechanical design interfaces are coordinated with process, civil/structural, electrical, instrumentation and controls, procurement, construction, and operations teams.
 Support project cost and schedule development by defining mechanical scope, identifying long-lead equipment requirements, reviewing quantities, and contributing to capital estimate and execution plan development.
 Support equipment procurement activities including preparation of technical requisitions, bid evaluations, vendor clarifications, and recommendation of awards.
 Resolve technical issues during study, design, procurement, construction, and commissioning phases.
 Support quality assurance and inspection planning for major equipment packages and mechanical installations.
 Provide oversight of design change management and ensure that changes are properly evaluated for technical, cost, schedule, and operational impacts.
 Support commissioning, start-up, and handover activities by ensuring mechanical systems are designed and delivered to meet operational requirements.
 Contribute to the continuous improvement of engineering standards, workflows, and project delivery practices within the organization.
 Mentor junior and intermediate engineers and provide technical coaching across the project engineering team.
 Perform other related duties as required.
 Participate in leading the (SME) project engineering team through project budget development, scope of work, WBS, schedule, commissioning plan, and estimating activities
 Qualifications 
 Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering required with Professional Engineer designation.
 Minimum 15 years of progressive mechanical engineering experience in industrial or process plant environments.
 Demonstrated experience supporting capital projects in mining, metals, hydrometallurgy, chemical processing, recycling, clean technology, renewables, or other heavy industrial sectors.
 Experience working on owner’s teams with EP, EPC, EPCM, and similar design build firms on industrial capital projects.
 Strong experience in front-end engineering, feasibility studies, design development, and execution support.
 Experience with detailed engineering, procurement support, construction support, and commissioning is strongly preferred.
 Familiarity with applicable codes, standards, and mechanical engineering design practices relevant to industrial facilities.
 Experience reviewing vendor packages, technical proposals, and contractor deliverables.
 Knowledge, Skills, and Competencies 
 Strong knowledge of mechanical engineering principles and industrial plant design practices.
 Strong understanding of rotating and static equipment selection, piping systems, utility systems, and mechanical design integration in process plants.
 Ability to evaluate engineering deliverables for technical completeness, quality, operability, maintainability, and fit-for-purpose application.
 Strong understanding of project delivery processes, stage-gate development, engineering assurance, and management of design risk.
 Excellent analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to assess technical trade-offs and support sound engineering decisions.
 Strong organizational and time management skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities across concurrent projects.
 Strong written and verbal communication skills.
 Strong interpersonal and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to work effectively across internal teams and external partners.
 Demonstrated leadership capability, including mentoring, coaching, and technical guidance of other engineers.
 Proficiency with Microsoft Office and familiarity with engineering document management and project systems.
 Ability to be flexible, agile, and able to pivot quickly in work execution approaches and delivery.
 Preferred Experience 
 Expertise in at least one of the following disciplines: hydrometallurgical, chemical processing, electrical, civil/structural, mechanical engineering, and/or recycling, critical minerals, metals refining, or similarly complex process-plant environments.
 Experience in brownfield and greenfield industrial project development.
 Experience working in start up organizations that focus on design optimization and refinement.
 Experience conducting targeted trade-off studies for the purpose of establishing critical engineering design criteria to retrofit existing plants and design new plants.
 Familiarity with North American codes, standards, and industrial permitting environments.

 $160,000 — $190,000 CAD

 MicroHabitat is seeking individuals to fill the position of Urban Farmer with ambition, leadership, and a passion for agriculture.
 Introduction:
 At MicroHabitat, we are pioneering urban agriculture to improve the urban environment, the lifestyles of city dwellers, and encourage a better understanding of environmental issues. We install rooftop gardens on businesses, institutions, and schools to reconnect people with nature and their food sources.
 What’s in store for you?
 A rewarding job where you can enjoy the summer and cultivate in unique locations.
 A competitive salary.
 Free coffee and tea, and a workspace in the heart of Vancouver.
 A team-focused work environment that encourages initiative and leadership.
 Happy hours and various social events throughout the year.
 Fun team-building activities with your colleagues — because MicroHabitat is first and foremost a big family!

We have the privilege of serving unique cities and aim to develop a team that reflects the diversity of these living and working spaces. Therefore, we encourage individuals from all backgrounds to apply and are committed to creating a space where everyone feels included, recognizing that this is an ongoing process.

 Setting up agriculture projects.

Legal Eagle? You get a strange amount of satisfaction from tightening a liability clause, spotting a hidden risk three sections deep, and finding a solution that protects the company without bringing business to a grinding halt. If you can turn complicated laws into practical advice, negotiate firmly without making enemies, and thrive in the fast-moving world of eCommerce, marketing, and consumer health, then you might have what it takes to join the legal team at AlgaeCal.
 Small Print ⇒ We’re looking for a commercially minded lawyer who can protect the business while helping it move forward. Someone who can review an influencer agreement in the morning, research a regulatory question before lunch, and calmly handle a demand letter in the afternoon without sending everyone around them into a panic.
 The good news? AlgaeCal has the world’s only clinically supported natural solution to this problem. We give hope to everyone worried about bone loss. As our Junior Legal Counsel, you’ll help protect that trust. Your work will support responsible growth, compliant innovation, and the ethical decisions that allow us to reach more people without putting our customers, our brands, or our business at unnecessary risk.
 If that excites you, you’ll find no better place to continue your legal career than at AlgaeCal. 
 This job might be for you if you… 
 Have in-house counsel experience. Haven’t got that experience yet? No worries! Articling students and recent law graduates are welcome to apply too.
 Know your way around a contract. You know that the danger in a contract is rarely hiding in the font size. It’s buried in the indemnities, warranties, termination rights, intellectual property provisions, and limitations of liability. You’ve drafted and reviewed commercial agreements before, and you know how to identify the terms that truly matter for the business rather than drafting for academic rigour.
 Understand how business actually works. You don’t practise law in a vacuum. You understand that the goal isn’t simply to eliminate every imaginable risk. It’s to understand the risk, explain the trade-offs, and help the business make a smart decision. You can protect the company without becoming the Department of No. Instead, you’ll work within a team where our approach is How Can I Help. 
 Can make complicated things simple. You can take a complex legal issue and explain it in plain English to someone who has never set foot in law school. You write clear contracts, practical memos, useful summaries, and recommendations that help people understand what they need to do next.
 You know when to push back. You can challenge unreasonable terms without turning every negotiation into a courtroom drama. You know when to stand firm, when to compromise, and when a seemingly small clause creates a much bigger business risk.
 You spot problems early. You naturally notice the legal and compliance issues other people miss. Whether you’re reviewing marketing copy, packaging, a product name, a supplier agreement, or a new business initiative, you know how to identify potential exposure early and recommend a practical way to reduce it.
 You provide solutions. You take the time to understand what another business unit or leader is trying to achieve, uncover the problem behind the request, and bring them a practical solution. You research the options, explain the trade-offs, and set out a clear plan that protects the business while helping everyone get to the best possible outcome. 
 You care about protecting great brands. Trademarks, brand assets, product names, licensing, co-branding, and enforcement all interest you. You understand how valuable a strong brand can become, and you want to help protect it. And if you’ve got experience in intellectual property law, we’ll probably swoon.
 You’re comfortable in regulated territory. You understand that consumer health businesses operate in a complex regulatory environment. FDA, FTC, advertising law, privacy, disclaimers, licensing, and cross-border requirements don’t intimidate you. Experience in supplements, healthcare, eCommerce, or regulated consumer products would make us especially excited to meet you.
 You know when to keep your mouth shut. You’ll have access to sensitive business, employee, financial, and legal information. You treat that access to confidential information seriously. You exercise sound judgment, adhere to your professional obligations, and understand that discretion is not optional.
 You’ve already earned your legal stripes. You’ve completed a Juris Doctor, Bachelor of Laws, or equivalent qualification. You also bring one to two years of in-house legal experience or comparable commercial legal experience.
 You don’t let the little things slide. You’re obsessed with accuracy. You double-check your work, question inconsistencies, and take pride in delivering advice that people can trust.

 You’re hungry to learn more

Providius is looking for a Software Engineer, Test to help build and maintain the automated testing behind our software products.

 This role sits within engineering. Testing is part of how we build software, not a separate step at the end of the development process.

 Our software analyzes live network and media traffic in complex, mission-critical environments. It runs primarily on Linux across physical servers, virtual machines, containers, and cloud environments.
 Testing these systems involves more than clicking through a user interface. You may be validating an API response, checking database data, replaying network traffic, investigating a Linux service, or determining whether an unexpected result came from the application or the environment underneath it.
 You will help build and maintain automated regression suites and the infrastructure that supports them, including fixtures, test data, captured traffic, mocks, and simulated inputs.

 Investigate flaky tests and help identify their underlying causes

 Test integrations such as APIs, syslog, SNMP, webhooks, and email notifications
 Assist with performance, load, and longer-running reliability tests
 Test installation, upgrade, and migration scenarios
 Debug failures across application, database, operating system, and network layers
 Work with developers to determine appropriate test coverage for new features

 Contribute to testing AI-enabled features when required

 Python, Java, and TypeScript
 pytest, JUnit, Playwright, and Cypress
 REST APIs
 PostgreSQL and TimescaleDB
 Linux
 Docker and virtual machines
 CI/CD pipelines
 JIRA and Bitbucket
 Network and time-series data

 This role is hybrid, based out of Vancouver, Canada or Toronto, Canada.
 Who You Are 
 You have 3+ years of relevant experience in embedded systems, firmware, systems software, hardware/software integration, or a related field, with a degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or equivalent practical experience.

 You understand computer and SoC architecture - including buses, memory systems, clocks, resets, and hardware interfaces - and can connect those fundamentals to observed system behavior.
 You have hands-on hardware bring-up and system-debugging experience using tools such as JTAG, UART, oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, or protocol analyzers; you also build tests, automation, and regression coverage.
 You work methodically through unfamiliar problems, use data to find root causes, and communicate findings while collaborating across hardware and software teams. Experience with pre-silicon platforms, interfaces such as PCIe or DDR, chiplets, RISC-V firmware, or shared test infrastructure is a plus.
 What We Need 
 Develop and execute silicon enablement tasks for IP, subsystems, SoCs, and SiPs, covering feature behavior, system integration, and product-level workloads.
 Design and maintain firmware, test software, scripts, utilities, and reusable enablement infrastructure using C/C++ and Python.
 Define and evolve enablement plans from feature requirements, architecture documents, and product use cases; identify coverage gaps and build tests to address them.
 Develop firmware and host software on simulation, emulation, or FPGA platforms and carry it forward into post-silicon bring-up and system operation.
 Bring up and debug hardware, investigate failures to actionable root causes, and work across design, verification, firmware, systems, and infrastructure teams to resolve issues and document results.
 What You Will Learn 
 Work across the silicon lifecycle, from pre-silicon planning and tapeout through board and system bring-up and ongoing product support.
 Build a broad understanding of how architecture, design, verification, firmware, systems, and product engineering come together to deliver first-silicon success.
 Use firmware, automation, instrumentation, and system-level debugging to understand silicon behavior in real products and turn findings into better designs.

In 1949, as Diners Club tells it, Frank McNamara finished dinner in Manhattan and found his wallet at home in another suit. His wife came down and paid. He returned to the same table the following February and settled the bill with a piece of cardboard, honored at twenty-seven restaurants and carried by two hundred people, most of them his friends. A year later there were 42,000.
 McNamara solved two problems at once. Acceptance: enough restaurants to make the card worth carrying, and enough diners to make it worth accepting. And credit: thirty unsecured days of it, on nothing but a signature. The networks settled acceptance decades ago. What is left is the credit, and the question of why someone carries this card rather than another one. That is this role.
 Mercury is building its first consumer credit card. We are looking for a Senior Product Manager to define what it is, ship it, and grow it from a first cohort into a portfolio. The scope is the credit account itself: the acquisition and application funnel, the approval experience and the underwriting decisions behind it, how the line moves over time, what the rewards are worth, and the experience of carrying the account day to day. 
 Key responsibilities: 
 Build a card people put at the front of the wallet and recommend without being asked
 Take the card from zero to launch: decide what ships first, and carry it through program setup and compliance sign-off
 Make the approval the clearest and fastest in the category: underwriting owns the model, you own the application, the wait, and the answer
 Own how customers experience their line: an increase that feels earned, a decrease that is explained 
 Own the proposition we take to customers, from rewards and redemption to pricing, and understand the economics that fund it
 Set the craft bar: sweat the details, copy, disclosures, latency, empty states, that decide whether a card feels inevitable rather than adequate
 Drive the use of AI where it makes the experience meaningfully better: spend that makes sense at a glance, problems surfaced before they are noticed
 Make correctness and trust product features: own balances, interest, minimum payments, and statements that reconcile, and be measured on them
 Grow the business: own acquisition, activation, retention, and the loops that compound, starting with the businesses Mercury already serves
 Align the ecosystem: bring engineering, design, data, risk, compliance, legal, marketing, support, and partners behind one cohesive plan for the card
 Some things that might make you successful in a role like this: 
 A consumer product manager with taste: you have launched products people chose to use, and can point to the decisions that made them work
 6+ years building consumer products, including at least one where money moved and errors were expensive
 Fluency in credit, or the capacity to acquire it fast: approval rates, line assignment, vintage curves, charge-off, interchange, and rewards liability
 An exceptionally high bar for craft, and a customer-centered, data-driven, and experimentation oriented approach
 You have shipped AI-led products to real consumers and have opinions about what AI makes possible and where it fails
 Exceptional cross-functional collaboration across engineering, design, data, risk, compliance, and partners

 Maintenir des graphiques de matériaux, des systèmes Niagara, des paramètres, des conventions de nomenclature et des configurations d’effets réutilisables propres, lisibles et bien structurés.
 Utiliser des outils tels que Photoshop, Substance Designer, Blender, Houdini, Maya, EmberGen ou d’autres logiciels selon les besoins pour soutenir la création d’effets.
 Gérer des configurations de matériaux complexes, des « Blueprints », des points d’ancrage de script, des événements d’animation, des déclencheurs liés à la jouabilité ou des besoins d’implémentation propres au moteur.
 Résoudre les problèmes liés aux effets visuels en partenariat avec les équipes techniques, d’ingénierie, de conception, d’animation, audio et autres disciplines.
 Maîtriser les bases de l’optimisation des effets visuels, incluant le nombre de particules, le surdébit, le coût des shaders, la mémoire des textures, les taux d’apparition, les paramètres d’évolutivité et les contraintes de performance de la plateforme.
 S’assurer que les effets sont lisibles, performants et alignés sur les besoins de jouabilité, la direction artistique, la dynamique, l’ambiance et les commentaires des joueurs.
 Passer en revue le travail des artistes internes, des studios partenaires ou des fournisseurs externes et fournir des commentaires clairs, constructifs et concrets.
 Aider à maintenir un seuil de qualité constant pour un ensemble d’effets, une fonctionnalité, un niveau ou une petite équipe.
 Soutenir la planification à court terme en aidant à décomposer les demandes d’effets visuels en tâches claires, priorités, dépendances, risques et critères de validation.
 Identifier de manière proactive les risques liés à la production, incluant les ancrages de jouabilité manquants, les pics de performance, une direction floue, les lacunes du processus, les problèmes de dépendance ou une exécution de styles incohérente.
 Travailler en étroite collaboration avec les concepteurs, les artistes conceptuels, les directeurs artistiques, les artistes techniques, les ingénieurs, les animateurs, les concepteurs audio et les producteurs.

 Solides compétences en création de matériaux et de textures avec des outils tels que Photoshop, Substance Designer ou des logiciels similaires.

**This is a 2 year term position, with possibility to extend**
 Position Context: 
 The Senior Functional Business Analyst will be fully dedicated to the University's ERP Modernization Program, with a focus on the Student Information Systems (SIS) project, and potentially support on the Finance Information System (FIS) project. This transformational initiative aims to modernize the technology, processes, and services that support the student lifecycle.
 The University's current ERP system, Ellucian Banner, has been in place for many years and includes significant customization. An ERP program is underway to modernize the system.  The Senior Functional Business Analyst will work closely with stakeholders to understand existing processes, identify underlying requirements, and distinguish business-driven needs from legacy practices.
 Working in partnership with Functional Analysts (FAs) and technical teams, the Senior Functional Business Analyst will develop a deep functional and hands on knowledge of Banner, including system configuration business rules, workflows and functional dependencies. The Senior Functional Business Analyst will actively participate in solution design, configuration, validation and troubleshooting, and will progressively develop the expertise required to support long-term functional ownership of the solution.
 This role requires an experienced professional with strong business analysis capabilities who can bridge business needs, operational processes and system functionality, understand cross-functional impacts, facilitate decision-making, and support stakeholders through organizational change. The Senior Functional Business Analyst will remain engaged throughout the project lifecycle, from business analysis and process design through solution development, testing, implementation, and business acceptance, ensuring that solutions meet intended business outcomes.
The Senior Functional Business Analyst will combine strong business analysis capabilities with hands-on functional expertise, translating business needs into practical system solutions and helping ensure that business processes and system configuration remain aligned.
 Main Responsibilities: 
 Develop a strong understanding of current student administration processes and the Ellucian Banner environment, including business rules, exceptions, dependencies and legacy customizations.
 Provide senior professional expertise in the examination and definition of objectives for existing and future systems.
 Work with stakeholders to uncover underlying business needs, challenge existing practices, and identify opportunities to simplify, standardize or redesign processes rather than replicate the legacy environment.

We're looking for a Senior Applied Scientist to own the intelligence layer behind our Parts Agent — one of the most strategic bets on our Inventory & EAM roadmap. The agent sits on top of a multi-layer parts data model (PartMaster, StockRecord, PhysicalInstance) and is responsible for answering hard inventory questions: when to reorder, how to optimize stock levels across sites, which parts are at risk of stockout, and how to reconcile messy supplier catalogs into a clean parts master. Your focus will be building the decision models, optimization routines, and AI-powered tools that make those answers trustworthy enough for enterprise maintenance teams to act on.
This is a high-ownership role. You'll shape the modeling approach, partner closely with product and design on what inventory managers actually need, and ship iteratively against feedback from real enterprise customers.

What you'll do

 - Own and evolve the optimization and ML models that power Parts Agent capabilities: reorder point prediction, economic order quantity, multi-site stock balancing, and demand forecasting.

 - Design and implement increasingly sophisticated inventory intelligence: vendor lead time modeling, criticality-weighted safety stock, substitution graph traversal, and proactive stockout alerting.

 - Build and maintain APIs and tools that expose these models to GenAI agent workflows (tool calling, structured input/output), enabling the Parts Agent to take grounded, explainable actions.

 - Partner with PM and design to translate messy real-world inventory problems into tractable models, and push back when "optimal" isn't what operators actually want.

 - Iterate with real users via design partnerships and pilot deployments. Take feedback from parts managers and procurement teams seriously and reflect it back into the model.

 - Contribute to the surrounding Python service: performance, observability, testing, and reliability of the inventory intelligence runtime.

 - Help shape how parts intelligence integrates with the broader MaintainX product over time, including learning from historical usage and purchasing data to continuously improve model inputs.

About you

 - 5+ years of professional software engineering or data science experience, with significant time spent on optimization, forecasting, or ML systems shipped to real users.

 - Strong fluency with at least one optimization paradigm (LP/MILP, stochastic programming, simulation) and practical experience with demand forecasting or inventory management models.

 - Solid Python service engineering: APIs, async, testing, profiling, observability. You can own a production service end-to-end.

 - Academic grounding in Operations Research, Industrial Engineering, Supply Chain, Statistics, or a related quantitative field; strong undergraduate foundation at minimum.

 - Track record of iterating data-driven systems with real users — you've felt what happens when a model recommendation gets rejected and you've redesigned the approach in response.

 - Product mindset and delivery orientation: you ship, you measure, you iterate. You care about the operator outcome, not just the metric.

 - Comfort with ambiguity. You can co-design the data model and feature schema with the team rather than waiting for a clean spec.

 - Familiarity with GenAI tooling (LLM tool calling, structured output, prompt design for constrained generation) is expected.

Nice to have

 - Experience at a known product company shipping inventory management, supply chain, or procurement optimization at scale.

 - Exposure to learning-augmented optimization — using historical purchasing or consumption data to estimate lead times, priors, or constraint weights.

 - Domain experience in MRO (Maintenance, Repair & Operations) inventory, spare parts management, field service logistics, or manufacturing supply chains.

 - Tech-lead experience or interest in growing into a tech-lead role on this team.

As Senior Manager, Billing Services & Support, you are ultimately responsible for the physicians, clinics and hospitals who count on Petal to get paid. You own the delivery of our billing services: every claim optimized and submitted accurately and on time, every payment tracked and reconciled, and clients who trust us with one of the most important parts of their practice. You lead a provincial team of Team Leads and Medical Billing Specialists (36 people) across our BC offices.
 This role has plenty of room to build. Our BC business is growing, with enterprise-level clients alongside our established physician and group clients, and our software keeps evolving. You will set the standard for how BC operates: clear expectations, metrics every leader owns, a team staffed for growth, and an engaged team that adopts new features and functionality with ease. Working alongside your peer managers across Canada, you'll help shape what great billing service looks like at Petal.
 You don't need to be a medical billing expert on day one. We will teach you the domain knowledge. You do need to be an experienced leader of leaders who brings structure, reads the numbers, and takes people through change with clarity and care.
 What you will own: 
 Client Service & Billing Delivery 
 Own the delivery of billing services for BC clients end to end: claims prepared and submitted accurately and on time, tracked through adjudication, and reconciled to payment.
 Make sure every physician, clinic and hospital gets a consistent, high-quality experience, whichever team or office serves them.
 Maintain clear billing guidelines and service levels for our clients, so they always know what to expect from us and what we need from them.
 Act as the senior escalation point for complex billing and client issues in BC, resolving them in a way that addresses the root cause.
 Performance & Service Quality 
 Own BC's service and operational metrics, including client volume, submission timeliness, claim acceptance and rejection rates, payment turnaround and cost to serve.
 Set clear goals with each Team Lead and review performance regularly, using data to spot trends early and act on them.
 Balance volume, speed, quality and cost, and understand the tradeoffs between them.
 Plan staffing and coverage to match client demand and growth, so the team is ready for peaks, absences and new client onboarding.
 Maintain quality-assurance practices that keep accuracy high and inform coaching and training.
 Talent & Team Leadership 
 Own talent for BC end to end: recruitment, onboarding, development, coaching and performance management, in partnership with our Talent and HR teams.
 Lead, coach and develop your Team Leads through regular 1:1s, team syncs and clear expectations: what needs to be done, why it matters, who owns it, when it's due and how we'll know it worked.
 Own formal people decisions for your group, including hiring, performance ratings and calibration, applied consistently against our job family frameworks.
 Build a strong leadership bench and career paths that help people grow with Petal.
 Champion employee engagement: build a team culture where people feel informed, recognized and invested in the success of our clients.
 Continuous Improvement & Consistency Across Canada 
 Collaborate with Billing Services managers in other regions, under the guidance of the Director, Billing Services & Support, Rest of Canada, to build and share best practices, SOPs and service levels that are consistent across Canada.
 Partner with Product and our CX Operations team to keep improving our software and workflows, bringing the voice of your team and our clients so we can automate more and keep service exceptionally high.
 Lead your team through new features, tools and processes, explaining the why so improvements land and stick.
 Keep BC's processes and documentation current, so knowledge is shared across the team.
 Look for opportunities to apply automation and AI to make the work simpler and the service better.
 Cross-Functional Partnership 
 Partner with Customer Success, who own client relationships and renewals, so that service delivery supports client health with BC physician groups and health authorities.
 Partner with Professional Services on onboarding new clients, bringing the operational view of what clients need to be successful.
 Represent BC operations in company-wide programs, including security and compliance work (e.g., SOC 2).
 Bring recommendations, not only problems: frame the issue with data, set out the options and tradeoffs, and propose a path forward.
 Required

 3+ years leading leaders (Team Leads or Managers) across multiple teams or sites, including recruitment, coaching, performance management and ratings.
 A track record of building KPI frameworks and staffing plans, and using them to run the business.
 Experience leading teams through significant process, technology or organizational change.
 Strong analytical skills; comfortable working with operational data in Excel, Power BI or similar.
 Ability to travel regularly to our offices on the Lower Mainland and Vancouver Island.
 Excellent written and verbal communication in English.
 Strong Assets 
 Medical billing, revenue cycle or healthcare administration experience; knowledge of BC's MSP billing rules is a strong asset.
 Experience working with health authorities or other public sector healthcare clients.
 Experience in healthcare technology, SaaS or a technology-enabled services business.
 Exposure to compliance or certification programs (e.g., SOC 2, ISO 27001, privacy and security audits).
 French (spoken and written).
